# Build a requested interface

Inspect the brief, target code, project instructions, existing design system, dependencies, and relevant behavior. Preserve facts and functioning features while making the visual or interaction changes the user requested.

For an open product decision, use [shape.md](shape.md) to resolve only the material unknowns. A clear brief or existing authorization does not require another confirmation round. Infer routine reversible choices from project conventions and continue the build.

Choose a direction consistent with the audience, task, and visual authority. For generated concepts or missing assets, consult [codex.md](codex.md) only when that work is needed. A present image tool does not mandate a palette image, mock alternatives, repeated approval gates, or a subagent.

Implement in the existing stack. Use real content and assets, preserve brand and translations, and check installed dependencies before adding imports. Keep semantic controls, accessibility, reduced-motion behavior, responsive layout, and relevant loading/error/empty states. Do not replace factual data or genuine imagery with invented proof or decorative simulation.

Inspect the affected rendered surface and primary interactions at representative sizes. Run appropriate existing project checks, fix observed defects, and repeat only checks affected by meaningful fixes or unresolved concerns. Report what changed, actual validation, and limitations. Complete the authorized implementation rather than stopping after a plan; a separately requested `shape` remains a planning artifact.
